profile.reading: Data Foundry is a privately held Texas colocation operator. This facility, Data Foundry 01 (also called Texas 1), occupies Building 1 at 4100 Smith School Road, Austin, Texas 78744, on the operator's Data Ranch campus, a named 40-acre site the operator's own data centers index page describes as also hosting the separate Data Foundry 02/Texas 2 building (Building 2 at the same street address) roughly 30 to 40 meters away, tracked separately elsewhere in this registry. The operator's own contact and facility pages describe Building 1 at 150,000 square feet total, comprising 130,000 square feet of data center space and 20,000 square feet of dedicated office space, and list SSAE, HIPAA, PCI DSS, AICPA, and ISO 27001 compliance for the facility. No MW or power capacity figure specific to Building 1 was published on the pages reachable this session. Data Foundry has operated in Texas for more than two decades, with its current portfolio concentrated on this Data Ranch campus (Buildings 1 and 2), a separate Austin facility (Data Foundry 00/Austin 1), and one Houston facility (Houston 2); unlike larger REIT-owned or private-equity-backed operators, Data Foundry remains an independent Texas company and does not file SEC disclosures, so this entry's specifications are sourced solely to the operator's own published materials. No year-opened date was located for this facility in sourcing reachable this session. Smith School Road sits in southeast Austin, a submarket that has drawn data center development in part for its distance from the downtown core's flood-prone areas and its access to major highway infrastructure. The Data Ranch campus name reflects the site's prior use, a common pattern in Austin-area data center development where operators have repurposed former rural or agricultural land on the metro's expanding edge rather than building on infill sites.

reading.body:
Data Foundry - Texas 1 publishes 130,000 square feet of technical space but no megawatt figure, placing it outside the 13 Texas facilities that disclose power capacity and account for 389 MW of tracked state capacity.

Floor area alone does not predict AI workload capacity. A facility of 130,000 square feet is substantial, not marginal, but watts per rack determine what compute density the building can sustain. Without a published power figure, Texas 1 cannot be ranked against peers in the state or assessed for suitability to training and inference loads that drive infrastructure demand.

The operator's specification page lists no certifications, no redundancy tier, and no details on grid connection or backup power. Austin's grid region has faced scrutiny for capacity and reliability, but this facility's resilience characteristics and utility arrangements remain unpublished. For readers evaluating AI infrastructure, Texas 1 is an established large building whose actual compute relevance cannot be determined from available data.
